speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; let's start by asking how long the bleeding has lasted since the extraction.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3; Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec; Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec; Fibrinogen_Level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an incorrect diagnosis; gastroenteritis is an infection of the stomach and intestines and cannot cause bleeding gums or easy bruising. Given your family history of similar bleeding issues and joint swelling, we need to investigate further. Can you tell me if you have ever experienced excessive bleeding after a cut or surgery in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency). The combination of lifelong easy bruising, family history, joint swelling (hemarthrosis), and excessive bleeding after minor trauma like tooth extraction in a male patient is classic for Hemophilia A, not gastroenteritis.
